answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The cedar multiplier is published, charged in vine, and juniper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 3320 identities would post 788 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
